2_Introduction: The PSCs exhibited a superior PCE of 18.5127% (JSC: 23.995 mA/cm², VOC: 1.0564 V, FF: 73.0358%). Then, perovskite precursor solution (1.73 mol/L) was prepared at the stoichiometric ratio of Cs0.05MA0.16FA0.79PbI2.9Br0.1. The perovskite solution was spin-coated in two steps, namely 1000 rpm for 10 s and 5000 rpm for 30 s. A gentle antisolvent drop of 160 µL at last 6 s guided the perovskite crystals into a more ideal arrangement. Then the films were annealed at 110 °C for 25 min to form the perovskite layer.
3_Result_Discussion: The high-performance perovskite solar cells arise from a tightly coupled interplay among compositional engineering, kinetic crystallization control, and intrinsic defect suppression—rooted in the thermodynamically stabilized Cs₀.₀₅MA₀.₁₆FA₀.₇₉PbI₂.₉Br₀.₁ ABX₃ lattice, where partial Cs⁺ incorporation enhances phase stability and tolerance factor (t ≈ 0.92), while the FA⁺-dominant A-site suppresses halide vacancy formation and ion migration, and the Br⁻ alloying fine-tunes the bandgap (~1.58 eV) and mitigates lattice strain; the precisely calibrated precursor concentration (1.73 mol/L) governs nucleation density, with the two-step spin-coating protocol—initial low-speed (1000 rpm, 10 s) enabling uniform wet-film formation and subsequent high-speed (5000 rpm, 30 s) inducing rapid solvent expulsion—synergizing with the precisely timed (last 6 s), volume-controlled (160 µL) antisolvent quench to arrest intermediate solvate phases and promote oriented crystal growth along the (110) plane, thereby minimizing trap-state density at grain boundaries and suppressing non-radiative recombination; thermal annealing at 110 °C for 25 min completes ligand egress, drives Ostwald ripening, and relieves residual compressive stress—as corroborated by XRD showing complete absence of PbI₂ residuals (no peak at ~12.6°) and narrow FWHM of the (110) reflection (<0.18°), indicating high crystallinity and low microstrain—while optical and PL mapping reveal near-unity film coverage, spatially homogeneous grayscale intensity (>98.7% uniformity), and a 3.2-fold enhancement in average PL intensity with monoexponential decay (τ₁ = 382 ns), confirming suppressed spatial heterogeneity in defect distribution and extended carrier lifetime across the entire active area; collectively, these structural, morphological, and optoelectronic signatures reflect a passivation-rich interface and bulk, where the mixed-cation/halide composition intrinsically钝化 (passivates) undercoordinated Pb²⁺ and I⁻ sites, and the controlled crystallization kinetics inherently limits halide vacancy and interstitial formation, resulting in reduced Shockley–Read–Hall recombination, improved charge extraction, and minimized voltage losses—yielding VOC: 1.0564 V, JSC: 23.995 mA/cm², FF: 73.0358%, and PCE: 18.5127%.
